- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the forecast horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral, especially in the first 5–7 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts often peak too high after recent spikes, then drop too sharply in later days.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model overreacts and forecasts higher than true outcome; reduce forecast by 2–5% for such periods.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-forecast, model fails to adjust downward quickly; apply a downward correction of 1–3% per day of negative sentiment.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices; apply a 3–5% downward adjustment for the first 10–15 days if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- Model ignores sentiment decay: if sentiment peaks then declines, forecast still holds high; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day of sentiment decline.
